root_idea.summary: A root principle of sinking into depth, disappearing below the surface, or becoming hidden from view.
root_idea.development: The central image of going into a depth extends to the earth swallowing something, lunar darkening, sinking or deep water in wells, and figurative states of deficiency, hunger, and abasement.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The single QAC group is an attested Form I verb with distinct Quranic sinking, swallowing, and lunar-darkening uses.

senses.definition: To cause a person, place, or thing to sink into and be swallowed by the earth.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative transitive construction, commonly with بِـ; the Quran applies it to people, dwellings, and the earth's swallowing of what is upon it.

senses.definition: To sink into the earth and become swallowed up or hidden within it.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive or passive-like earth-swallowing construction, describing disappearance below the ground rather than an agent causing it.

senses.definition: To become dark through eclipse or loss of light.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence concerns the moon becoming dark; the eclipse sense is distinct from physical sinking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a well or spring: to sink, collapse, or disappear into the earth, taking its casing or water with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a well or spring that goes down into the ground or loses its visible water; related adjectival forms describe such a well or spring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the eye: to sink or become depressed in the head, with its dark portion disappearing; transitively, to put out or blind the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of disappearance inward; the evidence includes both intransitive eye descriptions and the transitive construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A solar eclipse, the sun losing some or all of its light.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical usage reports differing conventions about whether خُسُوفٌ denotes partial or total loss and whether the term is preferred for the sun or moon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deficiency, imperfection, fault, or a low or base quality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of accepting or being content with something defective or inferior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leanness or emaciation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of bodies, people, camels, and sheep or goats; the evidence treats these as instances of the same lexical branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become altered, especially for the worse, in color, complexion, or aspect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a body or person whose appearance has deteriorated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become pierced or rent, or to make a hole in or rend something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive and transitive formulations describe the same rupture or perforation branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel: to cease giving milk after an abundant yield, especially in winter; adjectivally, a she-camel characterized by abundant milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records both the abrupt cessation after abundance and a related descriptive use for a milk-rich she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A convalescent person, recovering from illness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet for one who has recovered or is recovering from disease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well dug through rock to reach an abundant, copious, or inexhaustible water source; also the source or place from which well water issues.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may describe piercing rock to reach lasting water. Figuratively, a prolific source, such as a source of poetry, may be described in the same way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or cut off a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported figurative or extended transitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go without food or fodder; to be hungry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a beast confined without fodder, a person passing the night hungry, or drinking without eating; خَاسِفٌ can mean hungry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impose a degrading or difficult condition on someone; to humble, abase, or bring abasement upon him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom includes requiring someone to undertake an unwelcome or difficult affair and leaving him in ignominy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deep place or depression in the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use referring to depths in the exposed surface of the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud or cloud-bank bearing much water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported lexical description places it as appearing from the western or right-of-the-qiblah quarter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wrongdoing, injustice, injuriousness, or tyranny.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A further figurative development of the language of abasement and oppressive treatment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave a matter as it is.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression: دَعِ الأَمْرَ بِخُسْفٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The edible fruit called جَوْز, the walnut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal lexical item reported for the people of al-Shihr; the evidence notes a variant form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A soft or level tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually used in the plural for soft tracts or level expanses of ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad dates; alternatively, a palm tree bearing little fruit whose unripe dates turn bad.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is reported with variant vocalizations and an apparent dual form that need not be dual in meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A light, active, brisk, lively, or sprightly boy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical use specifically describes a boy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantival lexical designation with no further constructional restriction supplied.

cautions: The Quranic Form I occurrences include both an agentive construction causing something to disappear into the earth and an earth-swallowing or disappearance construction; these are lexical relations rather than merely tense variants.
Classical terminology for eclipse varies concerning whether خُسُوفٌ denotes partial or total loss of light and whether it is preferred for the sun or moon.
